meaning:
ἀεί, adv.,
[in LXX: Isa.42:14 (מֵעוֹלָם) 51:13 (תָּמִיד), Ps 94(95):10, al. ;]
ever;
1. of continuous time, unceasingly, perpetually: Act.7:51, 2 Co.4.11; 6:10, Tit.1:12, Heb.3:10.
2. Of successive occurrences, on every occasion (MM, VGT, see word): 1Pe.3:15, 2Pe.1:12.
† (AS)

elsewhere.note: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit! As your fathers did, so you do.
For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
One of them, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons.”
Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways.’
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility…
Therefore I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, though you know them, and are established in the present truth.
